# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Mar 26, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today, development focused on addressing a breaking change in `op-geth` related to `StorageKeys` values and opening new pull requests for a CL layer consensus mode feature and dependency updates. Several L2CM upgrade-related issues were closed.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

No completed work to report today.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
Two new pull requests were opened today:
- A new feature for a proxyd CL layer consensus mode was introduced in [#587](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/587).
- A dependency bump for `requests` from 2.32.4 to 2.33.0 in `/op-conductor-ops` was initiated in [#586](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/586).

## CLOSED ISSUES

### L2CM Upgrade System Enhancements
Several issues related to the L2 Contract Manager (L2CM) upgrade system were closed today, indicating progress in streamlining and improving the upgrade process:
- The issue for creating a Solidity script to generate deterministic JSON NUT bundles was closed by [#19248](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/19248) ([#18834](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18834)).
- Support for dev feature flags in the L2 upgrade system was implemented and the corresponding issue closed by [#19324](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/19324) ([#18838](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18838)).
- The addition of `just` commands for generating NUT bundles was completed and the issue closed by [#19248](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/19248) ([#18840](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18840)).
- A `just` command for running L2 upgrade fork tests was added, closing [#18841](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18841) via [#19464](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/19464).

## NEW ISSUES

### `op-geth` Breaking Change
A new issue was opened regarding a breaking change in `op-geth` v1.101701.0 where `StorageKeys` values are now `null` instead of `[]` ([#780](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/780)). This change affects how empty arrays are returned, potentially impacting systems relying on the previous behavior.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Flaky Test: `TestCLELDivergence` ([#19681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19681))
This flaky test, `TestCLELDivergence`, was closed today. The discussion revolved around whether the observed reset behavior was a bug or an expected part of the derivation pipeline. Initial investigation suggested it might be a real bug related to the CL-EL divergence not persisting as expected. However, further analysis indicated that the reset is likely part of the initial derivation pipeline lifecycle and not necessarily an issue during EL sync. A potential mitigation was to wait for op-nodes to complete their initial derivation reset before running the divergence test. The issue was ultimately closed with the understanding that `/report-flake` would reopen it if the flake reappears, avoiding a backlog of potentially fixed issues.

### Flaky Test: `TestPreinteropFaultProofs_TraceExtensionActivation` ([#19760](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19760))
This flaky test, `TestPreinteropFaultProofs_TraceExtensionActivation`, was opened and discussed today. The error indicates an unexpected execution revert. The root cause was identified as a nonce race condition during the `migrateSuperRoots` process, specifically between `transactions.SendTx` and `bind.TransactOpts` when calling `PendingNonceAt`. A proposed fix in `ethereum-optimism/optimism#19745` is expected to resolve this by replacing the multi-transaction pattern with EIP-7702 SetCode transactions, eliminating the nonce management complexity and transient ownership states that led to the race condition.

### Contracts: Prove withdrawals using chain-specific root claim ([#18517](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18517))
The discussion on this issue, which aims to ensure `OptimismPortal2.proveWithdrawalTransaction` uses `IDisputeGame.rootClaim(uint256)`, questioned whether it could be closed. It was noted that the approach might have changed, and the switch to `rootClaimByChainId` based on game type has been merged. Previously, the issue was moved to the backlog due to dependencies on `OptimismPortalInterop` changes and the U19 execution, with concerns about ensuring withdrawals continue to work immediately after the upgrade.

### [L2CM] Investigate adding an array of predeploys to increase upgrade safety ([#19260](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19260))
This issue, concerning the safety of L2CM upgrades, received a detailed update today. A "Missing Implementation Deployment in NUT Bundle" bug was identified and fixed by PR #19464. However, the investigation revealed a deeper structural pipeline gap: the lack of a centralized source of truth for implementations and automated completeness validation across multiple data structures. This creates a risk of silent failures in future upgrades. The report highlights that while PR #19464 adds fork tests that would have caught the immediate bug, these tests have limitations (e.g., only iterating proxies, not all implementations). A latent issue with `ConditionalDeployer` was also identified, where a similar structural gap could lead to a more severe failure mode if its bytecode changes in a future upgrade.

### Document interop tx pool eviction behavior on reorg ([#19351](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19351))
A question was raised regarding the behavior of interop transactions in the mempool during a reorg. Specifically, it was asked whether interop transactions that were already in the mempool should be explicitly dropped or if periodic re-evaluation handles this. This follows a change in `op-geth#772` where interop executing messages are dropped from the tx pool on any reorg.

### Remove Karst-specific upgrade transactions from GenerateNUTBundle ([#19369](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19369))
A comment was added outlining the necessary updates to `UpgradeUtils.getTransactionCount()` when removing the Karst-specific transactions. This includes changing `txnCount_` calculation and removing Karst-specific entries from NatSpec comments and the `GasLimits` struct.
